extracted.intended_audience: Department of the Navy commanders, public affairs officers (PAOs), and DON personnel responsible for community relations, public events, media embarks, and guest embarkation programs
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and operational criteria for planning, approving, and conducting Department of the Navy community relations (COMREL) events, public appearances, use/loan of facilities and equipment, fundraising restrictions, and civilian guest embarkation/visitation programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programs requiring higher-level approval
rubrics_metrics.description: (Enumerated program types) National and international programs or events to include conventions and meetings; liaison between DOD and Washington, D.C. offices of national NGOs; programs providing information or other support to national organizations; aerial reviews on military installations within the U.S. if the review involves more than one service and proposals for aerial, parachute, or simulated tactical demonstrations; sporting events including preseason/post-season or previously scheduled national sports and professional athletic events; events of professional, technical, or scientific interest when participation results in additional costs to the Government; appearance on regional or national broadcast media by Navy or Marine Corps performance units; programs requiring exceptions to DOD policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such programs often require referral/approval up the chain; requests for aerial events should use the current version of DD Form 2535; programs requiring exceptions to DOD policy must be specifically justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to government-wide charitable fundraising policy (CFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: All DOD components must conform to a government-wide charitable fundraising policy, per the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM), executive agent for government fundraising, and overseer of the annual Combined Federal Campaign (CFC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charitable and fundraising support is restricted beyond the CFC regardless of personal or collective views about its worth. Restrictions apply to any fundraising outside the CFC for any local, regional, national, or international charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on official endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD members shall not officially endorse or appear to endorse any non-Federal entity, event, product, service, or enterprise, including membership drives for organizations or fund-raising activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs and editors must avoid language/appearance that suggests DON approval or favoritism.

rubrics_metrics.name: No selective benefit from events
rubrics_metrics.description: Events may not support or appear to selectively benefit any individual group, charity, organization, political campaign, ideological movement, or commercial enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs shall ensure no selective benefit in publicity or participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-cause fundraising restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundraising events for a single cause are inconsistent with DOD policy, even when the prospective recipient is covered by the CFC or is an authorized component-specific campaign such as the Navy and Marine Corps Relief Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies even when funds are to be donated in whole or part to one or several CFC charities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted membership drives and emergency appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership drives are allowed only for: (1) The Combined Federal Campaign; (2) Emergency and disaster appeals approved by the OPM; (3) Navy-Marine Corps Relief Society and other service-specific, approved charities; (4) Other private organizations composed primarily of DOD members or their families raising funds among their own members for welfare funds (requires approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such events require approval by the head of the DOD component command after consultation with the designated agency ethics officer; includes most morale, welfare, and recreation programs regardless of funding source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteerism allowed in personal capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Volunteerism in a personal capacity and out of uniform is encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fundraising restrictions do not preclude individual volunteer activity for charities of choice, provided it is personal and out of uniform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on participating in fund-raisers for gifts to DON
rubrics_metrics.description: DON members shall not participate in fund-raisers for the purchase of gifts, real or personal property even when intended for presentation to the Navy or Marine Corps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such activity is explicitly disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual interest events — funding responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutual interest events are those in which both DON and a non-government individual or group derive benefit at no additional cost to DON. Civilian sponsors are required to fund additional costs of DON participation; the command’s normal costs cover continuing expenses that would exist regardless of the COMREL event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of additional costs: lodging, meals (or per diem), travel, logistical support, shipping exhibits, rental space, utilities, custodial services. PAOs shall ensure no selective benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community involvement expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: DON commands shall make every effort to involve all levels of the community in COMREL activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Civilian sponsors must be willing to underwrite additional costs; PAOs shall ensure no selective benefit; see Article 0704.6 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reimbursement and gift-acceptance restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations exist on authorized reimbursement methods. Reimbursement is by check, payable to the Treasurer of the United States. Individual reimbursement to DON members is prohibited without the commander’s permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reimbursement arrangements are discouraged; PAOs shall coordinate with command comptrollers and legal offices to identify appropriate 'in-kind' and other gift acceptance methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Installation MWR support constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments may support on-base COMREL events with concessions and other appropriate offerings provided that generating MWR revenue is not a primary objective of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MWR support is allowed only when revenue generation is not primary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No admission or fees at military installations
rubrics_metrics.description: Charging admission is prohibited. No charges or fees shall be imposed on the public by a military installation for admission, parking or viewing any activity. Citizens shall not be charged for photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition — applies to all COMREL events hosted on military installations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary interest events — limitations and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary interest events are those that exclusively benefit DON and for which all resources are provided by DON. Resources for primary interest events are approved by local commanders and shall be covered by the command’s Operations and Maintenance (O&M) fund account; duration normally shall not exceed three days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond programmed O&M funds, COMREL activities shall not involve additional costs to the Government, nor shall participation detract from operational missions. COMREL events require CHINFO, DIRPA or higher approvals; aviation performance teams must request policy exceptions through chain of command to CHINFO or DIRPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disaster assistance coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Navy and Marine Corps commands may offer and provide assistance to surrounding communities in the event of a disaster or other emergency that threatens human life or causes great suffering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands must coordinate with FEMA/DHS and other designated federal/state coordinating agencies; CHINFO/DIRPA and federal emergency agencies must be advised; overseas disaster assistance must be approved by Department of State and coordinated by the combatant commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency events — approvals and cost responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval from CHINFO, DIRPA, and in certain circumstances ASD(PA), is required for highly visible interagency programs. DON may join other federal agencies in official events such as interagency exhibits and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation shall not interfere with official DOD missions; support shall be provided at no additional cost to DON/DOD; the requesting agency is responsible for all associated costs including meals, lodging and transportation; any loan of equipment to a federal agency must be approved and the requesting agency pays for damages or repairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presidential authorization for cross-agency participation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the President determines an international fair, other event or display of U.S. economic, democratic or cultural progress will strengthen international relations, the President authorizes participation across federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASD(PA) will notify down the chain of command; participation authorized across federal agencies with notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gift acceptance and solicitation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance or giving of gifts or gratuities with monetary value in either a personal or professional capacity is strictly regulated. DON members and their families may not accept gifts or gratuities from prohibited sources; DON members may not solicit gifts or prizes for command events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers exceeding value limits in the Joint Ethics Regulation should be forwarded up the chain with description; gifts from foreign governments require special handling; consumable perishable items for MWR may be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Representation Funds (ORF) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: ORF is the only funding source within DOD for government-funded refreshments at ceremonies, government-funded meals for guests, and mementos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORF is limited, strictly governed and its use involves reporting and frequent audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process for use of facilities/materials (DD Form 2536)
rubrics_metrics.description: Event sponsors desiring military support for COMREL events will submit their requests (other than aviation) on DD Form 2536 to the nearest military installation, which will evaluate the appropriate level of support and forward requests up the chain of command if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support must be within the command's public affairs responsibility and the interests of DON; PAOs may offer guidance in completing DD Form 2536 but will not complete the forms for the requestor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for loan/use of equipment and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for use/loan: must not interfere with operational or training mission; equipment must be readily available within the command or obtainable from a nearby DON command and not obtainable from commercial sources; loaning commands must be willing to provide similar support to comparable events; support cannot result in potential danger to persons or private property; safety requirements shall be observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs and commanders must confirm availability and safety; consider insurance/claim risk against the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: No participation in programs intended to provoke controversy or imply endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: DON may not take part in programs intended to provoke controversy; which endorse or selectively benefit; or show preferential treatment of any private individual, special interest group, business, religion, ideology, commercial venture, political candidate or organization; or which are intended to increase sales and business traffic for a specific business or merchant association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that could imply endorsement or preferential treatment must be denied or referred upward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on support to fundraising and youth programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Support of fundraising events other than the Combined Federal Campaign is severely restricted. Support of youth programs is governed by special rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult supplemental guidance for youth program rules and ethics counsel for fundraising requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: No implied endorsement via support or use of uniforms/insignia
rubrics_metrics.description: Support will not imply endorsement of a commercial enterprise or a partisan political candidate. Commercial requests for use of uniforms and insignia require ASD(PA) approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer requests for commercial uniform/insignia use to ASD(PA) via CHINFO or DIRPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of open mess facilities — permitted categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of open mess facilities is permitted per NAVPERS 15951 for: (1) persons attending a professional or technical military seminar; (2) a civic group on an official orientation or indoctrination visit; (3) Navy or Marine Corps League, base community council or similar group (not to exceed one meal per quarter per group); (4) national youth group on an orientation or indoctrination visit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NAVPERS 15951 requirements and local approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loans between agencies and to law enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Loan of assets between agencies is allowed but must be considered on a case-by-case basis and shall be approved by CHINFO or DIRPA. Loans to law enforcement for protecting life, limb or property are allowed with appropriate approvals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participation shall be at no additional cost to DOD and shall not detract from DOD operational, training or other requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color, honor and color guard participation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint Armed Forces color detail will normally be used when DOD provides a display of colors for an authorized public event. The color guard used at events of purely DON participation will normally be composed of DON members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See supplemental guidance for composition, order of precedence and flags of foreign nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parade and public-event participation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ASD(PA) may authorize participation when events are on a national or international scale and ASD(PA) determines they are in the best interest of DOD and/or recruiting. Commanders may authorize participation in a local parade sponsored by the community (rather than by a single commercial entity) when its purpose is remote from business interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DON commands shall not participate in events conducted for the benefit of commercial enterprises; shall not participate in or support beauty contests, fashion shows and attendant ceremonies; limited participation in motion picture premieres may be authorized with ASD(PA) concurrence when the film was made with DOD cooperation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical performance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Military musical performances during public events that meet all other criteria of this chapter are limited to a short patriotic program or introduction ('patriotic opener'). Military musicians shall not compete with civilian musicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DD Form 2536 for all non-aviation support of COMREL events, including band requests, shall be completed by the requestor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech content and clearance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All speeches shall: (1) remain within the speaker’s purview, consistent with and cite sources and, for civilian employees, be in compliance with the Hatch Act; (2) be non-partisan and shall not imply any DON sponsorship, endorsement or agreement with partisan statements made by others; (3) be consistent with National / DON policy; (4) receive security and policy review; (5) announcements of reductions in force, facility closure or reductions of major contracts, must be cleared by appropriate authority through the chain of command.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs must screen requests and ensure speeches comply with Hatch Act and security/policy review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform restrictions for commercial use
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for commercial use of uniforms or insignia is normally not authorized and will be referred to ASD(PA) via CHINFO or DIRPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See references for more guidance on uniform wear; unresolved questions referred to ASD(PA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on use of the Official Navy Seal and Emblem
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of the Navy Seal is approved for DON purposes only. 18 U.S.C. prohibits use of the DON seal by anyone other than bona fide commands and activities of the DON and DOD where appropriate. SECNAVINST 5030.4A restricts the use of the DON seal to official use only and to the exclusive use of the DON and DOD. An optional graphic, the Navy emblem, may be used with permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethics regulations prohibit use of Government position/title/organization names in ways that would suggest Navy or Government endorsement. Any use of the Navy Emblem, logos, or other insignia should be accompanied with the prominent disclaimer: 'Neither the Department of the Navy nor any other component of the Department of Defense has approved, endorsed, or authorized this product [or promotion, or service, or activity].'

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations with community, professional and special interest groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Interaction between key command officials and local civic leaders and groups facilitates effective, positive and professional community relations. DON members should be encouraged to join local, civic and professional organizations at their own expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With exception of the National Capital Region, local commanders may deal directly with local and regional chapters of national organizations; consult supplemental guidance for further criteria on suitable participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to information requests from non-media entities
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs will respond promptly, accurately and completely to requests for information or to complaints from citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See supplemental guidance for more detailed guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and categories for visits, tours and embarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines types of visits: Public Visitation on Invitation of the Commanding Officer; Command Visit; Educator Orientation Visit; Congressional Visits; Friends and Family Visits; Media Embarkation; Guest Embarkations (including JCOC and Distinguished Visitors/VIP Tours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different visit types carry different coordination, approval and reporting requirements; media embarks fall under Chapter 5 (Media Embarks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tour and shipboard-visit best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for visits and shipboard tours: remind all hands they represent the Navy/Marine Corps; prepare briefings on local customs for foreign port visits; provide 'Welcome Aboard' brochures with photo and unclassified mission/history; prepare explanatory signs (bilingual overseas if possible); arrange opportunities for citizens to meet ship’s company; select and train tour guides based on appearance, enthusiasm, personability and speaking skill; use language-capable hosts for foreign visits; treat news media invited as guests as news media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides should be trained and briefed in advance; the commanding officer is responsible for control of photography aboard ship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and approval authorities for visits and embarkations
rubrics_metrics.description: General policy: news media embark coordination is in Chapter 5; Distinguished Visitor programs and corporate executives may be treated as distinguished persons in certain orientation contexts; correspondents handled per Chapter 5; security and policy review required prior to disclosure of sensitive information; Unified Commander may approve non-news-media public affairs embarkations and delegate authority; ASD(PA) coordinates with service all non-news-media embarkations requested by senior authorities; recruiting-related embarks handled per applicable directives; congressional visits require flexibility and OLA coordination; sponsor coordinates travel when embark/debark crosses commands; embarkation of civilian women governed by OPNAVINST 5720.2L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow chapter-specific procedures and notify/coordinate with CHINFO/DIRPA/ASD(PA)/OLA as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required pre-embark information for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants should be provided information prior to embarkation: statement of purpose of the embark program; authorization statement and reporting instructions; name and rank of commanding officer and any embarked flag/general officer; caution about guests' health; statement that tempo of operations can change scheduling; recommended wardrobe, passport and immunization requirements; availability of emergency medical/dental facilities and ship’s store; camera use policy (encouraged subject to restrictions); fund reimbursement policy (Navy has no authority to defray personal transportation/expenses and guests are responsible for extraordinary expenses); hazards warning; statement that acceptance implies understanding of limitations and arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as enclosure to embark invitation; commanding officer responsible for control of photography and for statements about reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: General policies for civilian guest embarkations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guests responsible for providing their own transportation and, because programs are conducted at no additional cost to the government, participants must reimburse the Navy for living and incidental expenses. One selection criterion is extent of involvement in civic, professional and social organizations; Distinguished Visitors are those who have not had substantial previous exposure to the Navy and have wide spheres of influence; embarks should include participants from a variety of racial and ethnic backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embarks should not normally include DV spouses unless the spouse is a DV in his/her own right; geographic rules govern Atlantic vs Pacific embarks; guests will be informed of security restrictions and photography rules; billets/meals privileges generally afforded; Navy Exchange privileges limited to emergent needs and limited souvenir items.
